summary: I audited the three areas against the code and against all 11 runs in artifacts/final_v6, re-deriving every number rather than reading stored ones. The pure information boundary is genuinely sound: I parsed every actor prompt in the corpus section by section and every single line is attributable to that actor's own private_context, own observed events, own decisions/intentions or own memories -- no shared_context, no resolution, no compiled question, no other actor's private_context, memories, decisions or intentions, no future-dated event, and no wake reason ever reaches an actor (0 residual 6-gram overlap after subtracting what each actor is entitled to). Actor/world separation, however, is largely unenforced: the identity check at trajectory.py:346 is gated on `did_it`, which line 255 sets only for `actor_intention`, so on the starting_event and pending_progression paths -- 73 of 195 committed events, 37% of the corpus -- the world may author a named person's voluntary choice with no check at all, and I committed "Bo reads Ada's proposal, decides to accept it, and sends Ada a reply agreeing to her terms" through that path with `by` honestly set to bo_ferrer and zero routings; on the one path where the check does run it is defeated by omitting `by`, writing `by: null`, or writing the attempting actor's id. `choice_returned_to_its_owner` fired 0 times in 11 runs. The sender-side guarantee the brief asked about does NOT still hold -- evidence_avoiding/e44 hands Dana, as authoritative observed fact, that her message was not delivered because Marcus's phone is off -- and the test named after that guarantee is dead code that asserts nothing. Replay is deterministic (identical across four PYTHONHASHSEEDs), deep-copied, non-vacuous and provably 0 model calls, and it detects deletion and reordering, but it cannot detect mutation or in-place forgery of the persisted ledger, and `evaluation/reverify_replay.py` reports `exact=True` on a corpus whose every event description and terminal record I rewrote.

findings.title: The actor/world separation check is inactive on the two trigger paths that produce 37% of committed events
findings.evidence: sworldmodel/semantic_runtime/trajectory.py:255 (`did_it = actor_id if trigger_kind == "actor_intention" else None`) and :346 (`if envelope is not None and did_it:`); artifacts/final_v6 -- 195 K_EVENT commits by trigger: actor_intention 122, pending_progression 64, starting_event 9, i.e. 73 committed with the check structurally skipped; 23 of those name an actor in `by`. artifacts/final_v6/lease_other_names/journal.jsonl e22 "Margaret opens the email from Jian Wei and reads the lease document" (by=margaret_thornbury, starting_event trigger, no routing) in a run that returned YES with only 1 of 2 actors ever consulted; artifacts/final_v6/feedback_deadline e-records from world_call c18/c36/c54/c58/c72/c102/c112 author Aline opening her inbox, leaving her office, walking back and resuming reading (by=dr_aline_mercier, pending_progression); group_coordination c66/c70 "Tomas opens the group chat"; holiday_deposit c107 "Dev opens the text message from Ruth and reads it"; holiday_deposit c350 "Marian Prowse answers her phone..." carries by=ruth_kelleher. `choice_returned_to_its_owner` appears 0 times across all 11 structural_refusals.jsonl.
findings.why_it_matters: The branch's central claim is that whose choice it is is now enforced by identity rather than by a reviewer, but the enforcement only exists while adjudicating an attempt. pending_progression is the single most frequent world trigger (266 of 459 calls) and it is called with an `actor_id`, so it is precisely where the world is invited to talk about a specific person; there, and on every starting event, the world may commit that person's decision as history before they have ever been consulted, and the judge -- which is never shown `by` -- cannot tell the difference. I reproduced the worst case with a fake transport: on the pending_progression path a full decision ("Bo reads Ada's proposal, decides to accept it, and sends Ada a reply agreeing to her terms", by="bo_ferrer", observed=true) commits with 0 routings before Bo's model is called once, and it is exactly the event the resolution asks for. A YES resting on it would be a YES for a decision no actor ever made -- the same failure class the deleted event reviewer was blamed for, relocated.
findings.suggested_fix: Apply the identity guard to every adjudication that names an actor, not only to attempts: on any trigger, if `by` is an actor other than the one whose attempt or attention was being adjudicated, route control to that person and commit nothing.

findings.title: Even where the guard runs, it is bypassed by omitting `by`, writing null, or naming the attempting actor
findings.evidence: sworldmodel/semantic_runtime/envelope.py:174 makes `by` optional (`by = proposed.get("by")`, defaulting to None = "the environment did it"); trajectory.py:347-349 computes `chooser` only when `envelope.get("by")` is truthy AND differs from `did_it`. Executable check with a scripted transport on tests/test_semantic_runtime.py's SCENE, world adjudicating Ada's attempt and returning "Bo reads Ada's proposal, decides it is worth doing, and replies to Ada accepting it": by="bo_ferrer" -> routed, not committed (correct); by omitted -> committed as e20; by=null -> committed as e20; by="ada_vance" -> committed as e20. In all three bypasses the resulting event's observed_by is ['ada_vance'], so the sender is also told Bo accepted.
findings.why_it_matters: `by` is a self-report written by the same model that writes the description, and the runtime treats its absence as an affirmative claim that no person acted. A model that never emits the field -- or that emits the id of the person whose turn it is, which is the id the prompt has just told it to use -- defeats the guarantee completely while looking compliant. The corpus shows the model does write `by: null` on the direct product of a person's attempt 6 times, so the omission path is not hypothetical, only benign so far. Because the check compares a label rather than the content, holiday_deposit c350 already demonstrates a description of Marian answering her phone shipped under by=ruth_kelleher.
findings.suggested_fix: Require `by` on every event (reject the envelope when absent) and, on an attempt adjudication, require `by == did_it` exactly -- treating null as a violation rather than as the environment.

findings.title: The sender still learns recipient-side delivery: the own-doing grant carries far-end state into the sender's observed record
findings.evidence: artifacts/final_v6/evidence_avoiding, event e44 (ledger event.fired seq 43: did_it=dana_whitfield, by=dana_whitfield, for=['marcus_bell'], observed=false; ledger record `journal.observed {actor: dana_whitfield, event_id: e44, source: own_doing}`): "Dana sends a follow-up message to Marcus: '...'. The message is transmitted and enters the network, but Marcus's phone is off, so it is not yet delivered." It appears verbatim under "WHAT YOU HAVE ACTUALLY OBSERVED" in Dana's prompts at 2026-09-10T08:00 and 2026-09-11T08:00 (actor_views.jsonl / actor_exchanges.jsonl), against a private_context that reads "She is unaware that Marcus is avoiding her or that he is on leave." Mechanism: trajectory.py:916-922 grants observation to `did_it` via journal.mark_observed(..., by_own_doing=True), and journal.py:95 deliberately skips the `actor_id in e["for"]` requirement for that grant, with no check on what the description contains.
findings.why_it_matters: This is the HIGH from merged main, alive in the frozen corpus by a different route. Narrowing the grant from `self_act_of` to `did_it` stops it being inherited down a consequence chain, but the direct product of "send a message" is written by the world as a single event that contains both the sending and the far-end delivery state, so the narrowing does not help. Dana is handed, as authoritative observed fact, the one thing the scenario stipulates she cannot know; in a run whose entire purpose is to test that a person with no evidence stays uninformed, the runtime informed her. WORLD_SYSTEM (world_mind.py:37) forbids exactly this phrasing and make_world_validator has no structural check for it, so the rule is prompt-only and was ignored twice in this one 3-event run (e19 and e44).
findings.suggested_fix: Grant the own-doing observation only when the event's audience does not exclude the doer, or split the commit so the doer observes an authored projection of their own act rather than the world's full description of where it landed.

findings.title: The test that certifies the sender-side guarantee is dead code and asserts nothing
findings.evidence: tests/test_runtime_completion.py:366-399 `test_the_sender_does_not_learn_the_recipients_attention` branches on `if "event_consequence" in user`, but `event_consequence` no longer exists as a trigger kind (the corpus contains only starting_event, actor_intention, pending_progression). I instrumented the test: the committed events are only ['Ada sends her prepared message to Bo.', 'Ada sends her answer to Bo.'], `far` is empty, and the sole assertion sits inside `if far:`. It passes unconditionally. All 85 tests in tests/test_semantic_runtime.py + tests/test_runtime_completion.py pass.
findings.why_it_matters: The one test written to prove the guarantee the brief asked me to verify has been silently disconnected by the deletion of the follow_up chain, so the green suite is evidence of nothing on this point -- while the corpus contains a live violation of the same guarantee. The companion test at :300 `test_the_world_cannot_author_another_persons_voluntary_choice` exercises only the honest-label case on the actor_intention path, i.e. the single configuration that works, and covers none of the four bypasses above.
findings.suggested_fix: Rewrite both tests against the surviving trigger kinds -- assert that an own-doing grant never carries a description of the recipient's state, and parametrise the separation test over by=null, by omitted, by=the attempting actor, and the pending_progression path.

findings.title: Replay cannot detect mutation or in-place forgery of the persisted ledger, and reverify reports the stored exactness as if it had re-derived it
findings.evidence: I copied artifacts/final_v6/lease_return, rewrote all 10 committed-event descriptions to "TAMPERED - Aisha never signed or returned anything" and rewrote every semantic.terminal_check / semantic.terminal_verification record, then ran `python3 evaluation/reverify_replay.py <copy>`: output `ok lease_return exact=True calls=0 events=10 integrity=ok`, exit 0. The kernel state_hash of the tampered ledger is byte-identical to the stored one (5a4b33f73437f3fb8d7cd401be3b95cfd505d891191df29df0c8cf774d9aa87f) because no semantic-runtime op has a reducer (journal.event, journal.observed, semantic.terminal_check, semantic.actor_call, semantic.world_call, semantic.attempt, semantic.horizon_reached are all absent from sworldmodel/world.py:_REDUCERS). evaluation/reverify_replay.py:33-35 copies `original.get("exact")` out of replay_verification.json, the sibling file in the same directory as the ledger it certifies; the CLI's own pass condition (:49-50) is only `not ledger_integrity and llm_calls == 0 and checked.events`. Direct probes on the disk-only path: mutate a description -> nothing detected; flip `observed` -> nothing; rewrite the final terminal to YES -> nothing; mutate a record timestamp keeping monotonicity -> nothing; delete a record -> detected (seq/cause); reorder -> detected (seq/cause); append a forged event + YES citing it -> detected only by a state_hash that changes because `version` counts records. artifacts/final_v6/FROZEN_SHA.txt names commit 6f3258d, and .gitignore line `artifacts/final_v*/*/` means the 11 run directories are untracked -- `git ls-files artifacts/final_v6/` returns only the 3 top-level .txt files -- so git provides no content binding either.
findings.why_it_matters: "11/11 replay exact" is the headline that makes the corpus reviewable, and it is not a re-derivable property of the corpus: it is a boolean in a file next to the ledger. The one conjunct that covers the trace-only records, `records_match`, needs the live world, which existed only inside the run process; after the run there is nothing independent to compare against and no hash over the records. Every number under review -- 209 events, 8 YES, 0 NO_AT_CUTOFF, 14% machinery -- rests on untracked files whose contents cannot be checked by the tool the repo offers for checking them, and whose certificate is editable in the same edit.
findings.suggested_fix: Store sha256(canonical_json(records)) (and a per-run ledger digest) in the run artifacts and in a tracked manifest, and have reverify recompute and compare it instead of copying `exact` forward.

findings.title: The ledger integrity check's own-doing exemption lets a forged observation of any event by any actor pass
findings.evidence: sworldmodel/semantic_runtime/replay.py:87-95 -- `elif d.get("actor") not in ev.get("for", []) and d.get("source") != "own_doing"`. Probe on artifacts/final_v6/lease_return: appending `{"op": "journal.observed", "data": {"event_id": "e11", "actor": "tomas_herrera", "source": "own_doing"}}` yields `ledger_integrity: []`; the same record with `source: "observed_via:eX"` is correctly caught ("records 'tomas_herrera' observing e11, which never reached them").
findings.why_it_matters: The exemption is keyed on a free-text string, so the only integrity rule that guards the information boundary in the ledger is switched off by writing four words. Since observed_by is what the judge reads and what build_view feeds an actor, a forged own-doing observation both informs a person of something that never reached them and can turn a NO into a YES, while the corpus's integrity check reports 'ok'.
findings.suggested_fix: Accept source='own_doing' only when the event's attempt_id names a semantic.attempt record whose actor is that observer.

findings.title: A model-written free-text string is injected into the actor prompt on the continuity-correction path
findings.evidence: sworldmodel/semantic_runtime/trajectory.py:478-481 appends `contained(verdict['reason'])` to the actor's prompt; it happened 20 times in the corpus (e.g. feedback_deadline/dr_aline_mercier: "The evidence shows Aline resumed reading at 13:06 and was still reading at 13:36, so she could not have finished and sent comments before that time."; anti_stereotype/ethel_pomeroy: "...(current time 7:02am Thursday) without acknowledging that she is speaking to the rep now..."). Every injected string matched a recorded semantic.continuity_review reason (0 mismatches), and 2 further prompts carried llm.py's `YOUR PREVIOUS REPLY WAS REJECTED` schema echo. This contradicts sworldmodel/semantic_runtime/views.py:25-28, which states "There is no free-text channel into a view... callers pass event ids, not prose, so nothing the world wrote can enter a view".
findings.why_it_matters: It is the only unstructured channel into an actor's context, and the code's own comment at trajectory.py:459-461 records that this reviewer previously "invented calendar facts and fed them back into the person's next prompt". The reviewer sees only that actor's view, so the blast radius is bounded, but the docstring asserts a property the code does not have, and any fabricated detail it emits is presented to the person as an authoritative correction.
findings.suggested_fix: Either drop the reason from the retry prompt (re-ask with the same view) or restrict the injected text to a fixed vocabulary of defect codes chosen by the validator.

findings.title: `by` is never persisted on the committed event, so the separation invariant is unauditable from the journal and invisible to the judge
findings.evidence: sworldmodel/semantic_runtime/journal.py:55-63 -- commit stores event_id, description, for, observed, source, attempt_id, trajectory_id and drops `by`; journal.events() (:132-136) does not project it; journal.jsonl keys across the corpus are ['attempt_id','cause','description','event_id','for','observed','observed_by','seq','source','t']. resolution.py:700-705 / :745-749 show the judge and verifier only `event_id, t, description, for, observed_by`. `by` survives only inside the copy of the queue payload in the event.fired record.
findings.why_it_matters: Whose choice a committed event was is the one thing this design elevated to a code-owned identity field, and it is not in the authoritative history. A reader of journal.jsonl -- and both readings of the record that decide the answer -- cannot tell an event the world attributed to a person from one it attributed to the environment, which is how the 23 world-authored person-actions in the corpus read as ordinary history.
findings.suggested_fix: Persist `by` in the journal.event record, project it in events(), and show it to the judge and verifier.

findings.title: `follow_up` is still required of the world and read by nothing
findings.evidence: sworldmodel/semantic_runtime/envelope.py:165-167 validates it and :199 returns it; world_mind.py:154-160 spends a paragraph instructing the model on it and :249 carries it into event_checked; trajectory.py stores it in the queue envelope and never reads it (no occurrence outside the envelope/world_mind pair). The prompt tells the model "When it is false, nothing further is asked", which is not true of this runtime.
findings.why_it_matters: The world is asked, on every judgment, to compute a field that decides nothing, and is told a false fact about the consequence of its answer -- which shapes how it writes the event it does emit. It is also the residue of the deleted transport chain, so its presence suggests to a reader that the chain still exists.
findings.suggested_fix: Remove `follow_up` from the envelope, the validator and the world prompt.

findings.title: build_view's own-actions projection lacks the trajectory scoping that journal.events() has
findings.evidence: sworldmodel/semantic_runtime/views.py:57-60 selects OP_ACTOR_CALL records by `r["data"]["actor"] == actor_id` only, with no trajectory_id filter, whereas journal.py:120-122 explicitly scopes events by trajectory_id for exactly this reason.
findings.why_it_matters: Latent rather than live -- every run in the corpus is single-trajectory -- but if a world ever held two, an actor's "WHAT YOU HAVE ALREADY DECIDED AND TRIED" section would carry their decisions and intentions from the other trajectory, and replay's views projection would carry them too.
findings.suggested_fix: Filter the own-actions projection by journal.trajectory_id the same way events() does.

findings.title: check_ledger_integrity collapses duplicate event ids, so a substituted event id is not flagged
findings.evidence: sworldmodel/semantic_runtime/replay.py:78-79 builds `by_event` as a dict comprehension keyed on event_id; a second record with the same event_id silently overwrites the first, and nothing asserts that event ids are unique or that they follow the `e{version+1}` rule journal.py:54 uses to mint them.
findings.why_it_matters: Combined with the mutation blindness above, a forger can duplicate an existing event id on a rewritten event and have every id-existence check (observations, terminal citations) resolve against whichever copy came last.
findings.suggested_fix: Add a uniqueness check on journal.event ids to check_ledger_integrity.
